---
title: "Auditing calibration feasibility before trusting weights"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Auditing calibration feasibility before trusting weights}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r}
library(calibcheck)
M <- rbind(c(1,0),c(0,1),c(1,0),c(0,1))
f <- check_feasibility(M,c(.9,.1,.1,.9),target_num=c(9,1,1,9),target_den=10)
f[c("status","scope","lower","upper","exact")]
f$certificate[c("lower_num","lower_den","upper_num","upper_den")]
```

The columns have identical patterns across the two margins. No nonnegative
normalized weights can attain conflicting targets. A producer's success flag
is not a feasibility certificate. The exact bracket uses independently verified
integer witnesses; it proves infeasibility at the requested tolerance for the
specified rational target, not merely that the LP implementation reported failure.

```{r}
audit_calibration(M,c(.9,.1,.1,.9),raw=c(.1,.9),converged=TRUE,
                  margin=c("A","A","B","B"),level=rep(c("1","2"),2))$raw$ledger
```

Feasible does not mean practically usable. A target may require almost all
weight on a single observation. Box constraints change the attainable set.

```{r}
M <- matrix(c(1,0,0,0),1)
check_feasibility(M,.97)$min_max_weight
check_feasibility(M,.97,upper=.5)[c("scope","status","lower","upper")]
```

The four-task target requires at least 97% on the first task at exact balance;
with a 50% cap the discrepancy is at least 0.47. The bounded result is numerical,
not an exact certificate. Base weights can be translated into normalized per-task
lower and upper bounds if that is the intended domain; no distance-to-base-weight
objective is implemented.

```{r}
z <- calibration_matrix(data.frame(region = c("a", "a", "b")),
                        list(region = c(a = .5, b = .25, c = .25)))
audit_calibration(z$M, z$target, raw = c(1, 1, 1),
                  margin = z$margin, level = z$level)$raw$ledger
```

The missing level is retained rather than silently dropped. The target mass
assigned to it is a lower bound on the residual. Bounded concentration is
computed over individual weight caps, not just aggregate pattern counts.

The public tests use synthetic matrices, exact target counts and independent optimization oracles.

## Limitations

The exact verifier currently uses bounded integer arithmetic, not arbitrary
precision. For large target denominators, a 2^20 witness can be insufficient
at tolerance 1e-6; the automatic routine retries at 2^31 and larger safe scales.
Arbitrary binary floating-point targets can exceed the cap; no rational target
is silently approximated. A numerical verdict and a certified verdict are
distinguished by `exact` and the certificate field. Exact zero discrepancy is
not guaranteed by finite witness rounding. Bounded problems are numerical only.
